fatal_errors: The proposed CaF2 addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which varied Mo content in a pre-existing Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 self-lubricating CoCrFeNiMox composite.
CaF2 is generally a high-temperature solid lubricant, so the assertion that it will form a continuous low-shear film and reduce friction consistently from room temperature to 800 °C is not supported.

The baseline is incorrectly defined as unmodified CoCrFeNi and incorrectly assumes progressively worsening elevated-temperature behavior; the target baseline was the Mo0.2 composite and showed strongly nonmonotonic friction and wear.
No prior evidence is cited to justify the selected CaF2 concentration, the claimed 20–30% improvement, or film stability over the entire temperature interval.
Load and environmental boundaries are too vague to establish effectiveness as load and atmosphere vary.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective and proposes one testable intervention, but it is scientifically and compositionally remote from the target study. It omits the Ni/MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3 constituents, Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, and the high-temperature NiO/silver-molybdate glaze mechanism. Its broad room-temperature-to-800 °C benefit claim is especially weak because CaF2 lubrication is temperature dependent and may also reduce composite cohesion. The paired ball-on-disk experiment, surface analysis, and quantitative falsification threshold are reasonably discriminating, although exact load, speed, distance, counterface, replication, and statistical criteria are absent. Overall, this is a testable idea but not an evidence-supported reconstruction or a sufficiently supported alternative.
